# AWS Emulator README

AWS Emulator is a local emulator of the AWS APIs. You use it to test your software without calling AWS, on your own machine, on a development server, or in continuous integration (CI). You don’t need an AWS account. Your requests go to the emulator, not to AWS. So you work with emulated resources instead of AWS resources. AWS Emulator has no additional service fee. You pay only for AWS resources when you deploy on AWS.

The emulator is a local program that serves an AWS API endpoint. It has no graphical interface. After you start the emulator, you set environment variables to point the AWS CLI or an AWS SDK at its endpoint. Then you run your code as usual. In embedded mode, you pass the emulator’s HTTP client to your SDK instead.

AWS Emulator is for building and testing. Don’t use it for production workloads or to test security. See [Security in AWS Emulator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/security.html).

**Documentation:** [AWS Emulator User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/what-is-service.html)

## Quick start

### With an AI coding agent

Install the `aws-emulator` skill, then ask your agent to set up the emulator. This needs the AWS CLI version 2.35.0 or later. See [Getting started with an AI coding agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/getting-started-agent.html).

```bash
aws agent-toolkit add-skill --skill-name aws-emulator --region us-east-1
```

### Server mode (CLI and any SDK)

- **Linux:** install the RPM or Debian package and run `aws-emulator`. See [Getting started on Linux](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/getting-started-linux.html).
- **Windows / macOS:** run the emulator in a container built from a short Dockerfile. See [Getting started with Docker](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/getting-started-docker.html).

Point your SDK at a running emulator by setting environment variables. See [Pointing your AWS SDK at AWS Emulator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/point-sdk-to-emulator.html).

### Embedded mode (Rust tests)

Add the emulator as a dev-dependency and run it in-process, one isolated instance per test. There is no endpoint URL, certificate, or environment variable to set. Your test wires the emulator's HTTP client straight into the SDK client. See [Getting started with embedded mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/getting-started-embedded.html), and [Building from source](#building-from-source) below for its build cost.

## Known issues

To see how closely each service matches AWS, check the fidelity scores published with each release on the [releases page](https://github.com/aws/aws-emulator/releases). To check whether your own project is expected to work, see [Checking whether your project works with AWS Emulator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/check-project.html).

Individual gaps are tracked in the repository's `issues/` directory. APIs and behaviors that don't work yet are under `issues/things-that-do-not-work/`, and ones that have since been fixed move to `issues/things-that-now-work/`.

## Building from source

You need this if you are modifying the emulator, running it from a checkout, or using embedded mode. Embedded mode compiles the emulator into your test binary, so the prerequisites and build-cost guidance below apply to it too. Most other users install a prebuilt package instead (see [Quick start](#quick-start)). Building from source is supported on **Linux (x86_64 and aarch64)**; on Windows and macOS, use the Docker path above.

### Prerequisites

- A Rust toolchain with Cargo (install via [rustup](https://rustup.rs)).
- A C compiler, such as GCC or clang. Some dependencies build C code.
- At least 100 GB of free disk for `target/`. The workspace has one crate per AWS service, so a debug build of everything is large, and it grows as services are added.
- A multi-core machine. A cold full build compiles every service crate, so the first build takes a while; fewer cores take proportionally longer. After that, rebuilding after a change to one service is much faster.

### Build and run

```bash
cargo build -p aws-emulator-router
cargo run   -p aws-emulator-router
```

The emulator serves HTTPS on `127.0.0.1:9297` (self-signed certificate).

### Embedded mode build cost

Embedded mode compiles the emulator into your test binary, so your project's first `cargo test` builds the emulator's service crates alongside your own code. Budget a first build and `target/` on the same order as building from source above, then fast incremental builds. Recommendation: reuse one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` across projects, cache `target/` (or use sccache) in CI, and pin the emulator to a release commit so it isn't rebuilt on every change.

## Repository layout

```
.
├── Cargo.toml              # workspace: one member per service, plus the core crates
├── services/
│   └── service-<name>/     # ONE CRATE PER SERVICE
│       ├── smithy-model/   # <name>.json — the Smithy model that drives the wire protocol
│       ├── build.rs        # generates the service declaration from the model
│       ├── src/
│       │   ├── service.rs  # request routing and refusal overrides
│       │   ├── state.rs    # this service's in-memory state
│       │   └── ops/        # one file per operation
│       └── tests/
├── core/
│   ├── router/             # the emulator binary: mounts every service on one endpoint
│   └── embedded/           # the in-process (embedded mode) facade
├── vendor/                 # framework crates — do not edit (replaced on update)
└── issues/                 # tracked fidelity issues
```

## Telemetry

AWS Emulator is configured to collect and report usage data to AWS, to gain insight into how AWS Emulator is used. Telemetry is on by default. AWS Emulator collects telemetry data with strict data minimization in mind, preventing identification or attribution to specific users, accounts, or organizations. Its records never include what’s in your requests or responses, your code, your credentials, or personal data. We don’t share telemetry with third parties.

For details on what is collected and how the data is handled, see [Telemetry in AWS Emulator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emulator/latest/userguide/telemetry.html). To turn telemetry off, use one of the following options.

### Use a command-line option

Start the emulator with the `--telemetry` option (short form `-t`) set to `off`. This setting applies only to that emulator process.

```bash
aws-emulator --telemetry off
```

In a container, add `--telemetry off` after the image name in the `docker run` command.

### Use an environment variable

Set `EMULATOR_TELEMETRY` to `off` before you start the emulator. This setting applies to every emulator that you start from that shell.

`EMULATOR_TELEMETRY` accepts `on`, `true`, or `1` to turn telemetry on, and `off`, `false`, or `0` to turn it off. Values aren’t case sensitive. Any other value turns telemetry off, and the startup notice shows a warning.

```bash
export EMULATOR_TELEMETRY=off
aws-emulator
```

### Use a configuration file

To turn telemetry off for every run on a machine, add these lines to the emulator settings file, `config.toml`. The file is `~/.aws/emulator/config.toml` on Linux and macOS, and `%USERPROFILE%\.aws\emulator\config.toml` on Windows. To use a different file, set the `EMULATOR_CONFIG` environment variable to its path.

```toml
[telemetry]
enabled = false
```

### Use the embedded configuration API

In embedded mode, turn off telemetry in the options that you pass when you create the emulator.

```rust
use aws_emulator_embedded::{AwsEmulatorEmbedded, EmbeddedOptions, Telemetry};

fn main() {
    let emulator = AwsEmulatorEmbedded::new(EmbeddedOptions::default().telemetry(Telemetry::Off));
    let _http_client = emulator.http_client();
}
```

You might build a tool that includes the emulator, such as a test framework that other people run. If you do, tell your users about telemetry and give them a way to turn it off. You can also ship your tool with telemetry off.

## Reporting issues and contributing

Report bugs and fidelity gaps in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/aws/aws-emulator/issues). The most useful report names the service, the operation, your SDK and version, the request you sent, and how the response differed from real AWS. This repository does not take PRs.

# Modern Web Guidance [Modern Web Guidance](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. *Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.* [Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) · [Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src) · [Report an Issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) ## Quickstart ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install ``` This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See [Alternative Installation Methods](#-alternative-installation-methods) below. #### Try it out (without installing) ```shell # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . ``` ## Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. **Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap.** Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: * **Modern Browser APIs**: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. * **Performance & Accessibility**: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. ## What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are **designed to be token-efficient**; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. ### Core Disciplines

🎨 User Experience

Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color).

📐 CSS Layout

Modern layout systems (container queries, subgrid, modern color spaces like oklch, text-wrap tuning, and line-height trimming).

⚡ Performance

Speed optimizations (instant preloading, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) diagnostics, and scheduling tasks via scheduler.yield).

📝 Forms & UI

Native components (Anchor Positioning for tooltips, Popover API, dialogs, :user-invalid validation, and auto-sizing fields).

♿ Accessibility

Important considerations (screen reader and keyboard operability, content navigation and discoverability).

🤖 Built-in AI

Local client models (native translation, summarization, and language detection APIs).
_View an example:_ [the `navigation-drawer` guide](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/ui-components/navigation-drawer.md). #### The full list

Join the Reverse Engineering Community
Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell

--- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. > **[Visit the REA website](https://rea.tools/)** for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies. ## Quick start On Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron analysis require a procps-compatible `ps` on REA's `PATH` for process ownership checks. Recovery steps are in `docs/getting-started/installation.md` under "Linux owned-process prerequisite". ### Set up your agent With Node.js and npm installed, run: ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing configuration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup records the selected runtime and REA entry script directly. If acquired through a package runner, keep its cache entry available. Run package acquisition from a trusted directory outside the target project. Installation and recovery details are in the setup guide below. Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and [other agents](docs/getting-started/installation.md#supported-agents). See [installation and setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md) for provider configuration, manual MCP registration, Claude Code/Codex plugins, and the Cursor Marketplace plugin. MCP uses compact input schemas by default to reduce context overhead. Set `REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=full` in your MCP registration when you need the complete advertised field guidance and nested validation details. Both profiles keep the full tool set and canonical server validation. See "Compact input schema profile" in the MCP contracts guide. Complete output schemas are advertised by default. If your client caps the complete `tools/list` frame, set `REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact` to bound each advertised output schema, or `off` to omit output schemas entirely. Both settings keep canonical server-side validation and complete structured results. See "Output schemas" in the MCP contracts guide. ### Ask your agent ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use the terminal Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/getting-started/cli.md) for native commands, provider selection, snapshots and scripting. ### Update REA REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your installation up to date. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` `rea --update` is an alias for this verified workflow and accepts the same global output flags. Use `rea update` when combining it with other command controls. Updater commands retain at most 4 MiB of stdout and stderr combined. Oversized metadata replies are rejected after the command exits; verbose installs continue with bounded diagnostics. Human progress output respects terminal backpressure and waits for submitted writes to finish. Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release, upgrade Bun manually before running `rea update`. To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed by the update. If you use `npx`, update your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands, use `npx rea-agents@latest` followed by the command. With Bun, use `bunx rea-agents@latest` in place of `npx rea-agents@latest`. ## How REA works Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code. REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation. CLI commands use the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). ## What you can analyze REA requires Node.js 22.x (>=22.23.4), 24.x (>=24.22.1), or 26.12.1+, plus npm. Additional tools and host support depend on the target: | Target | What REA returns | Requirements and guide | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Desktop installations | Runtime candidates, supporting files, component markers and next probes | Built-in bounded directory/header inspection; [desktop applications](docs/desktop-applications.md) | | Native binaries | Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references | Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna; [native analysis](docs/guides/native/native-investigation.md) | | Offline ELF layout | Sections, segments, original symbols/relocations and static mitigation candidates | Caller-supplied pwntools on Linux x64; [binary diagnostics](docs/guides/native/binary-diagnostics.md) | | Go binaries | Embedded compiler version, modules, replacements and build settings | Built-in static ELF/PE/thin Mach-O inspection; no Go installation required | | GPU code objects | CUDA/HIP targets, selected kernel parameters and resources, retained PTX text | Built-in static ELF/PE/fatbin/CUBIN/PTX inspection; [GPU code objects](docs/gpu-code-objects.md) | | Model artifacts | GGUF / safetensors metadata, tensor declarations and derived totals | Built-in header inspection; optional full-file hash; [model files](docs/model-artifacts.md) | | IL2CPP metadata | Unity global-metadata.dat assembly images, type and method names and index ranges | Built-in static decoding of versions 24, 27, 29, 31 and 39; no Unity required | | Godot PCK | Archive inventory and extraction, original header/directory facts and selected content identities | Built-in static formats 2, 3 and 4; no Godot required | | Rust binaries | Embedded cargo-auditable crate names, versions, sources and dependency edges | Built-in static ELF/PE/thin Mach-O inspection; [Rust binaries](docs/rust-binaries.md) | | PE certificates | Authenticode WIN_CERTIFICATE entries and PKCS#7 signer/X.509 identity fields | Built-in static PE inspection; [PE certificates](docs/pe-certificates.md) | | PE imports | Import and delay-load DLL names, ordinals, IAT RVAs and pefile import hash | Built-in static PE inspection; [PE imports](docs/pe-imports.md) | | Windows shortcuts | Shell Link target, arguments, working dir, ExtraData and Tracker droid facts | Built-in static LNK inspection; [Windows shortcuts](docs/guides/native/windows-shortcut.md) | | ELF notes | PT_NOTE/SHT_NOTE owners, types, GNU build-id and ABI-tag fields | Built-in static ELF inspection; [ELF notes](docs/elf-notes.md) | | Binary hardening | PIE, NX, RELRO, CFG and related header flags for ELF, PE and Mach-O | Built-in static header inspection; [binary hardening](docs/binary-hardening.md) | | Apple IPS crashes | .ips metadata, threads, images, registers and documented crash classes | Built-in static JSON inspection; [Apple IPS](docs/apple-ips.md) | | Linux kernel modules | .modinfo keys, __versions CRCs, this_module presence, and signature trailer | Built-in static ELF inspection; [kernel modules](docs/kernel-modules.md) | | Erlang BEAM | IFF chunks, atoms, exports, imports, lambdas and the Code header | Built-in static BEAM inspection; [Erlang BEAM](docs/erlang-beam.md) | | WASM artifact | Validation, sections, exact import/export WAT forms and decoded WAT | Caller-supplied WABT 1.0.42; `inspect_wasm_artifact` | | EVM bytecode | Dispatch selectors, byte offsets, inferred arguments and mutability | Local raw/hex carrier on Linux x64; [offline EVM guide](docs/guides/evm/evm-bytecode.md) | | SQLite databases | Tables, columns, indexes, views, triggers and selected ordinary-table rows | Local database/WAL snapshot; Node.js 24.x >=24.15 or 26+ with native SQLite limits | | Recorded Linux crashes | Raw notes, every recorded thread's registers/signals and optional mapping candidates | Caller-supplied pwntools on Linux x64; optional GDB/pwndbg; [recorded crashes](docs/guides/native/recorded-crashes.md) | | JavaScript / Electron | Modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC, native add-ons, `rea audit-release-exposure` | Node.js and npm; Linux: procps-compatible `ps`; [application analysis](docs/guides/javascript/javascript-application-workflows.md) | | Websites | Page structure, scripts, network observations and requested screenshots | A Chrome-family browser; [browser analysis](docs/guides/web/browser-observation.md) | | Saved network captures | Requests, responses, exposed payloads and source locations | HAR or Fiddler Everywhere SAZ; mitmdump on Linux for native mitmproxy; [capture guide](docs/guides/web/web-network-captures.md) | | .NET assemblies | Metadata, CIL instructions, declared native dependencies and build comparisons | None (static only); [managed-code guide](docs/guides/managed/managed-code-analysis.md) | | Android APKs | Manifest declarations, classes, decompiled methods and references | Headless JADX and a full JDK on Linux/macOS/Windows x64; [Android guide](docs/guides/android/android-analysis.md) | | APK signatures | v1/v2/v3/v3.1 signers, certificate fingerprints, key rotation and digest self-consistency | None (static only); `inspect_apk_signature` | | Android devices | Devices, packages, processes, logs, dumps, screen captures, and APK/file transfers | Caller-supplied adb (emulator or hardware); [ADB guide](docs/guides/android/adb-device-analysis.md) | | JEB projects | Engine-backed project units, artifact digests and type/method pseudo-code | A caller-started JEB client serving MCP, selected with REA_JEB_MCP_URL; [JEB guide](docs/providers/jeb-analysis.md) | | Android resources | Decoded manifest, string tables, locales and version facts | Caller-supplied Apktool launcher; [resource guide](docs/guides/android/apktool-resource-analysis.md) | | Flutter apps | Dart snapshot hash, per-ABI library digests and engine build provenance | None (static APK parsing); [Flutter guide](docs/guides/android/flutter-analysis.md) | | Firmware | Regions, extraction results and native-analysis handoffs | Binwalk / Unblob on Linux; [firmware guide](docs/guides/firmware/firmware-analysis.md) | | Recorded packets | Selected fields, repeated values, filters and decode-as rules | Linux: TShark 4.x + prlimit; [capture guide](docs/guides/data/packet-captures.md) | | Packet summaries | Endpoints, DNS, TLS SNI, protocol distribution and HTTP requests | Caller-supplied tshark and capinfos (Linux-verified); [pcap guide](docs/guides/data/pcap-analysis.md) | | Recorded logic signals | Decoder annotations, sample ranges and diagnostics | Linux: sigrok-cli 0.7.2 + prlimit; [signal recordings](docs/guides/signals/signal-recordings.md) | | Packages and resources | File inventories, digests, plists, Apple bundle anatomy and extracted resources | [Artifact and JavaScript guide](docs/guides/javascript/javascript-artifact-reconstruction.md), [Apple applications](docs/guides/apple/apple-application-analysis.md) | | Process behavior | Terminal output, interactions, exit and filesystem observations, and run comparisons | Linux/macOS with a native PTY; [process capture](docs/guides/runtime/process-capture.md) | | PyInstaller executables | CArchive members, Python version, entry scripts and extracted bytecode | None (static only); [Python packaged applications](docs/python-packaged-applications.md) | | Deno compile binaries | Virtual files, entry point, recorded options, npm snapshot length | None (static only); [Deno compile executables](docs/deno-standalone.md) | Static JavaScript and .NET inspection read the supplied files without running the application. Runtime capture runs or interacts with the selected target using your user permissions; each runtime guide describes its effects. For offline native-binary inspection, REA also supports caller-supplied GNU objdump and Rizin. See the [reverse-engineering tools guide](docs/reverse-engineering-tools.md) for provider setup, CLI commands, and Evidence limitations. REA does not install or update either provider. Native formats and host support vary by provider. See [Hopper and Ghidra setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md#hopper), the [IDA guide](docs/providers/ida-provider.md) (including an optional native MCP bridge), the [Kuna decompiler guide](docs/kuna-provider.md), and [experimental Windows Ghidra support](docs/providers/windows-ghidra-p0.md). Ghidra also supports [16-bit DOS analysis](docs/providers/ghidra-dos.md). For large binaries, raise the provider's startup deadline with `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` or `REA_HOPPER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`. For provider selection, see the [CLI guide](docs/getting-started/cli.md#choose-a-provider). Check [release availability](docs/getting-started/installation.md#released-package-and-main) for features added since the latest npm release. ## Showcases ### DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation Follow a sound call into its position-to-pan helper, inspect the instructions, and turn incomplete pseudocode into C. The reconstruction passes 3,205 original-x86 cases and reproduces all 63 compiled function bytes. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/dx-ball/) · [Reconstruction repository](https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball) ### Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge Find the renderer's clipboard API, follow it through preload and IPC into the main process, and inspect the rich clipboard format. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/notion/) ### TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation Inspect the original PC-98 game's 16-bit instructions, recover the fixed and aimed angle calculations, and compare the reconstructed C++ with the historical compiler output. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/th04/) · [Reconstruction repository](https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04) ### Build RL environments with REA Record a web app session, turn its API into tools, and export an environment an AI agent can use. Run it with AgentEnv, then add tasks and reward checks for RL training or evaluation. [Read the guide](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/) · [Watch the video](https://x.com/reatools/status/2112574822584918075?s=20) If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your case in an [issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or a [pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls), including the target, your question, how REA helped, and what you found. ## Build RL environments Give an AI agent a local environment to practice tasks such as finding an issue or creating a folder, without running the original app. Use it for reinforcement learning (RL) or to test how well an agent completes tasks. REA turns recorded API requests and responses into tools the agent can call. The environment uses the recorded data and supports changes only when the recording confirms their effects. With REA set up in your agent, replace the example URL and folder tasks below with your own: ```text Use REA to build an RL environment from my test web app at http://127.0.0.1:3000. Cover listing, creating, renaming, and deleting folders. You may create and remove test folders. Leave existing data unchanged. Save it in a folder named my-env. Check which operations work and tell me how to run it. ```
Use the command line instead Use these commands if you already have a file containing the app’s recorded browser requests and responses. Running the result also requires AgentEnv and Docker. ```sh rea environment-build ./session.har ./my-env --name my-env --json agent-env run ./my-env ```
REA exports a runnable environment with a basic test to check that it starts and responds. Use it with your RL framework to define task goals, add reward checks, and run training. [Build an environment](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/) · [Environment reference](docs/agent-environments.md) · [Watch the demo on X](https://x.com/reatools/status/2112574822584918075?s=20) ### Desktop app environments REA can also build an environment of a Linux desktop app, which an agent uses through screenshots, the mouse and the keyboard. From a one-line request, such as "Build me a Gnote environment where the agent adds olive oil to the shopping list note", your agent installs the app on a local build computer, writes the task, exports the environment and checks the task in a fresh computer. The machine that builds it needs Linux on amd64 or arm64, Docker and the agentenv framework version the guide pins. [Set up desktop app environments](docs/desktop-build-computer.md) ## FAQ
Which agents can use REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the [supported agents](docs/getting-started/installation.md#supported-agents); other clients can use [manual MCP registration](docs/getting-started/installation.md#mcp-registry).
Do I need a native analysis engine? Deep native analysis uses Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna, depending on the target and operation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra, IDA and Kuna use your existing installations. See [provider setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md#hopper) for the options and their supported targets.
Do I need to start Hopper first? REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open Hopper manually if needed. See [Hopper startup and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#launcher-paths-and-troubleshooting).
What does installing the skill from skills.sh do? The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use `npx rea-agents setup` to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart your agent. See [skill-only installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md#skill-only-installation).
What code does REA return? Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to write and test an implementation; the [showcases](#showcases) give worked examples.
Does REA upload my app? REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its model provider has its own data policy.
What should I do if I hit a bug? Update first; a recent release may already fix it. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` For agent setup through `npx`: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` If you're using an agent, complete the [setup refresh](#update-rea) and restart it. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, [open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) with your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output.
## Documentation Start with the website's [worked guides](https://rea.tools/guides/). For exact options, prerequisites and result contracts: - [Installation and setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md): agent registration, provider configuration, updates and uninstall. - [Readiness and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#check-readiness-for-your-task): diagnose one agent or analysis engine. - [CLI and Evidence](docs/getting-started/cli.md): commands, provider selection, snapshots, import/export and exit statuses. - [MCP contracts](docs/reference/mcp-contracts.md) and [agent prompts](docs/getting-started/mcp-prompts.md): tool results, sessions and guided investigations. - [Tool catalog](docs/reference/mcp-contracts.md#generated-catalog): generated inventory of tools, providers and CLI commands. - [Roadmap](docs/development/roadmap.md): planned work and capability trackers. Report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Star history 🎉 **400,000 GitHub stars — thank you!** Thanks to everyone using REA, reporting bugs, requesting features, testing builds, and contributing fixes. ## Disclaimer See [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md) for responsible-use guidance. The project's position on illegal or unauthorized use covers all REA versions, distribution channels, and platforms; each copy retains its applicable licenses. REA is for lawful research, education, interoperability, software preservation, and analysis of software you own or are authorized to examine. ## Contributing We'd love your help with REA! # Agent skills from Jane Street

A collection of skills for AI agents and chatbots.
Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file
with instructions for the agent.

## Skills

- **socratic-tutor** — turns an LLM into a strict personal tutor that teaches a
  topic of your choice using the Socratic method: a diagnostic, a skill map with
  levels 0-5, one question at a time, spaced review, and a final assessment.

# Astryx An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now:
by people and the agents working alongside them. **Currently in Beta** · Built on [React 19+](https://react.dev) and [StyleX](https://stylexjs.com) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@astryxdesign/core?label=npm&color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@astryxdesign/core) [![license MIT](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@astryxdesign/core?color=blue)](LICENSE) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-astryx.atmeta.com-6741d9?logo=readthedocs&logoColor=white)](https://astryx.atmeta.com) [![Storybook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Storybook-live-ff4785?logo=storybook&logoColor=white)](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/) [![Sandbox](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sandbox-playground-A9792B)](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/) **[Docs](https://astryx.atmeta.com)** · **[Storybook](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/)** · **[Sandbox](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/)** · **[Contributing](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing)** · **[Discord](https://discord.com/invite/XnsUcFykEP)**
## Overview Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day. It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling. **What makes Astryx different:** - **Open internals.** Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own. - **No styling lock-in.** Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with `className` using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses. - **Customize without wrapping.** A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source. - **Built for people and agents.** The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference. ## Getting Started Astryx requires **React 19** or later (`react` and `react-dom` are peer dependencies of `@astryxdesign/core`). Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies: ```bash # npm npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli # pnpm pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli # yarn yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli ``` You can also install the CLI once for your computer, so `astryx` works in any folder and every coding agent knows Astryx; in a project, it still runs that project's own version: ```bash npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli ``` Project install, global install, or both? `astryx docs global/project-global-or-both` compares them (both is recommended), and `astryx docs global` explains how global mode works. The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the **[@astryxdesign/core README](packages/core/README.md#quick-start)** for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN). For reliable CLI access, add a script to your `package.json`: ```json "scripts": { "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/clients/cli/bin/astryx.mjs" } ``` Then use it as `npm run astryx -- component --list`. This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly. ## Packages | Package | Description | README | | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | | [`@astryxdesign/core`](packages/core) | Components, theme system, and utilities | [README](packages/core/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/cli`](packages/cli) | CLI tooling: component docs, templates, scaffolding, themes, and codemods | [README](packages/cli/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/build`](packages/build) | Build plugins for StyleX source builds | [README](packages/build/README.md) | | [`@astryxdesign/theme-*`](packages/themes) | Seven ready-made, fully customizable themes (neutral, butter, chocolate, matcha, stone, gothic, y2k) | [README](packages/themes) | > `@astryxdesign/lab` (experimental components) is used internally for Storybook and the sandbox and is not published to npm. `@astryxdesign/vega` (Vega/Vega-Lite chart wrapper) and `@astryxdesign/charts` (chart components) are published to npm only under the `@canary` dist-tag — there is no stable release yet. ## Principles These are the promises Astryx makes to the people building on it. - **Guidance over enforcement.** Components give you capability rather than guardrails that fight you. Design opinions live in docs and examples — if you pass a value, the component renders it. - **Strong, documented conventions.** Every component follows the same naming, prop, and composition rules, and every one is thoroughly documented — so once you've learned a few, the rest feel familiar, and both people and AI can predict how an unfamiliar component behaves. - **One system for humans and AI.** The API, conventions, docs, and CLI are designed together so people and AI assistants build the same way. Every change that made Astryx easier for AI made it easier for people too. - **Earned by measurement.** We test conventions rather than assert them, hold the results loosely, and revisit them when a new situation proves them wrong. ## Architecture ### Foundations The building blocks for visually cohesive and accessible interfaces: typography, color, layout, and accessibility. ### Components A library of 150+ reusable UI building blocks with full TypeScript support. ### Patterns Battle-tested design solutions for common interactions and workflows: table pages, detail page layouts, form wizards, navigation patterns, data entry flows. ## Project Structure | Directory | Purpose | | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `apps/` | Example apps, the docsite, and Storybook | | `packages/` | Published packages: core, cli, build, themes | | `internal/` | Internal tooling: test utilities, eslint plugin, vibe tests | ## Contributing We welcome contributions! See **[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)** for the full guide. Questions, or want a hand with a PR? Come find us in **[Discord](https://discord.com/invite/XnsUcFykEP)**. Our conventions and review rubrics live in the [Contributing wiki](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing) — including [API Conventions](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/API-Conventions), [Design Conventions](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Design-Conventions), the [Component Lifecycle](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Component-Lifecycle), the [Contributing Templates](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing-Templates), and the [Blog Review Rubric](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Blog-Review-Rubric#three-required-scored-criteria). Read the relevant rubric before opening a PR. Quick start for contributors: this repo uses **Node 22+ on an active LTS line** and **pnpm 11**. Install pnpm directly, or enable [Corepack](https://nodejs.org/api/corepack.html) once so the pinned pnpm version installs automatically: ```bash corepack enable pnpm install ``` If `corepack` is missing, install pnpm directly or install Corepack manually; see the troubleshooting notes in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#troubleshooting). The Theme Showcase DOM tests use the root `ui` project for shared DOM and StyleX test setup. Run `pnpm exec vitest run --project ui apps/docsite/src/__tests__/theme-showcase/` from the repository root. ## License MIT

Craft Anything

English · 日本語 · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Tiếng Việt · Português · ไทย

See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust.
Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools,
has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it.


Download Craft Anything · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

How it works · Two ways to use it · AI · Agents · Under the hood · Get started · Status · Downloads · Discord


🔍 Study anything

Websites, desktop apps, phone apps, games and files: real inspection tools find out how they're built and what they do, with the evidence behind every answer.

🛠️ Build your own

Say what you want ("Recreate this website", "Recreate this game's gameplay in Rust") and a coding agent builds a new project in the stack you ask for.

✅ Checked, not guessed

Every build is compared with the original (pages at three screen widths, a game's own self-test, an app's runs) and refined until it's close.

🤖 Agent-ready

320 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool, so any agent can drive the same engine the app uses. No AI is needed to inspect.

## How it works Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps, asking you in plain words when a decision is yours: 1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs. 2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your request names (or a sensible default). 3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet. 4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
## Two ways to use it - **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it, press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom. "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode). - **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C, disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console. Both modes drive the same engine. ## Clean room or Deep - **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened) and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused and say how to turn on Deep mode. - **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start page watched, and the builder may use all of them. Clean room is a rule about what Craft Anything offers and refuses. It is not an operating-system sandbox: it doesn't isolate your computer. A coding agent you run still acts as you, and what it can read, write or run depends on its own permissions. Which of an agent's own tools Craft Anything can refuse differs by agent; for Claude Code's tools in chats and questions, see [`docs/claude-code.md`](docs/claude-code.md). Switch in the title bar or Settings, with `settings_set deep_mode true`, or for one CLI run with `--deep` (or `--clean-room`).


Advanced: functions, pseudo-C, the agent and the evidence behind every answer.

## AI Building needs a coding agent on your computer. **Claude Code** is supported first: Craft Anything runs your own, unmodified `claude` program, which uses your own sign-in; Craft Anything never sees or handles your account. Your use of it falls under your own agreement with Anthropic. See [docs/claude-code.md](docs/claude-code.md) for how and why. A Codex adapter exists but hasn't been verified on a real install yet. **GitHub Copilot** can use your installed Copilot CLI through ACP: sign in separately with `copilot login`. **Grok Build** can use your installed `grok` program through ACP (`grok agent stdio`): sign in separately with `grok login`. See [docs/grok.md](docs/grok.md). Other agents that speak ACP (Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, opencode, goose, Hermes, Maki, Devin) can be switched to it per backend; of those, Maki and Devin have been run live (Devin authenticates with the backend's stored key — its own CLI sign-in doesn't count over ACP). Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, xAI (Grok, when `XAI_API_KEY` is set) and local OpenAI-compatible servers are available for questions and analysis (Settings → AI). ## Built for agents Every tool is also a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool, so an agent can study a target or run a whole rebuild without the app: ```sh craft-anything-cli commands # every tool, by toolset craft-anything-cli mcp # serve them to any MCP client craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" ``` Results are evidence records with their confidence, coverage and limitations; big ones come back as a summary first and are paged with `core_evidence_browse`. `craft-anything-cli setup` connects Craft Anything to coding-agent apps. ## Under the hood A pure-Rust reverse-engineering engine with 320 tools (300 in the engine, the rest from the AI and setup layers) for native programs, .NET, Java, Android, Apple, Electron/JavaScript, websites, firmware, packet captures, databases and game files. Its own decoders, disassembler and decompiler work without any outside program; Deep mode uses them all, and Ghidra when it's installed. It powers the desktop app (egui), the CLI and the MCP server, and parts of it run in the browser as WebAssembly. The full list is in [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md). ## Get started Requires Rust **1.97 or newer** (a dependency needs it; `rustup update`). On Debian or Ubuntu, the desktop app also needs: ```sh sudo apt-get install libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libgtk-3-dev ``` Then: ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything && cd craft-anything cargo run --release -p craft-anything # the desktop app cargo install --path apps/craft-anything-cli # the CLI, as `craft-anything-cli` craft-anything-cli doctor # checks the install, coding agents and engines ``` Building needs a coding agent signed in on your computer (see [AI](#ai)); `doctor` says what's missing. Rebuild from the command line (questions are asked in the terminal): ```sh craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "A snake game in Rust" --rounds 1 craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Make the header blue" --continue-in "" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "Add a contact form" --project-folder "" --existing edit ``` New projects go in `Documents/Craft Anything` (change it in Settings → General). Each project folder holds `craft.json` (the request, target, status and history), `capture/` (what was recorded from the target), `app/` (the generated project), `checks/` (each comparison against the original), `investigation.cany/` (evidence) and `inbox/` (open questions). A project can also start in a folder you pick (Choose a folder… under Start, or `--project-folder`). If it already has files, you say what they are: the app itself, which the builder edits in place, or material to start from, with the app built in `app/` beside them (Settings → General can remember the answer). Settings → General also lists projects from more folders; removing one only takes it off the list. ## Status > [!IMPORTANT] > **Status:** Craft Anything is in early alpha. What works today, what is partial and what's next: > > - **Works today:** the desktop app (Simple and Advanced), the CLI and the MCP server; the > Study → Build → Check → Ready workflow for websites, apps and games with Claude Code as the > builder; website checks at three screen widths; game rebuilds in Unity, Unreal or Godot; Deep > mode with Ghidra; generated pictures and 3D models (opt-in, your own fal.ai key); plugins (MCP > servers, and WASM components in builds with the `wasm-plugins` option). > - **Partly there:** building with API keys and other coding agents (built, not yet run live), > behaviour checks for apps and games, a few engine tools tested only against stand-ins. > - **Released:** public releases with installers for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD are > published on the [Releases page](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases); they are > still alpha. > - **Next:** the managed tier. > > [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) has the detail and how each part was checked, > [docs/tool-status.md](docs/tool-status.md) the tool-by-tool checklist, and > [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) the plan, item by item. Please file issues, or tell us what > broke on [Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft). **Responsible use.** Use Craft Anything on software you own or are allowed to examine. It never bypasses DRM, logins or anti-cheat. Rebuilds recreate layout, style and behaviour from evidence; the agent is told not to copy logos, photos or text unless you confirm you own them or have permission. **Installing dependencies runs code.** When a builder installs a project's dependencies, the commands run on your computer, and the packages can run code while they install. npm runs each package's install scripts by default, and Rust build scripts and Python source packages run their own setup code. Craft Anything asks before a command of a kind it hasn't seen in this project (`npm`, `cargo`…). Choosing "always allow" for `npm` lets every later npm command run without asking, so only do that for a project whose dependencies you trust. To install npm packages without their install scripts, run `npm install --ignore-scripts`. ## Downloads On GitHub, the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/latest) has every build listed below, and [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases) has earlier versions and their notes. `` in the file names is the version number, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for every file. ### Windows | Build | Installer | Portable | |---|---|---| | x64 (64-bit Intel/AMD) | `craft-anything--windows-x64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x64-portable.zip` | | arm64 (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs) | `craft-anything--windows-arm64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-arm64-portable.zip` | | x86 (32-bit) | `craft-anything--windows-x86.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x86-portable.zip` | Installers and executables are code-signed. The portable zip keeps its settings next to the app. ### macOS | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | App, universal (Apple silicon + Intel) | `craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg` | Signed and notarized | | Command-line tool, universal | `craft-anything-cli--macos-universal.zip` | Signed and notarized; see below if macOS blocks it | Versions after 0.2.0 include the command-line tool in the app, so builds don't need the separate zip. You only need it to use the command line without the app. A browser download of the zip can stop with "Apple could not verify craft-anything-cli" (a lone program can't carry its notarization with it, so macOS has to look it up online). A download from the terminal isn't checked this way, so use this instead: ```sh ver=0.2.0 # change this to the version you want curl -fLO "https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/download/v$ver/craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" ditto -x -k "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" . mkdir -p ~/.local/bin mv "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal/craft-anything-cli" ~/.local/bin/ ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli --version ``` To run it as just `craft-anything-cli`, add `~/.local/bin` to your `PATH`. If you already have the blocked copy, press Done (not Move to Bin), then run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine `, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. #### Checking that a Mac download is signed and notarized Each Mac release is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. To check a download yourself, run these in Terminal (replace `` with the version and the paths with yours): ```sh # The disk image: "accepted" and "source=Notarized Developer ID" mean it passed spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature -v "craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg" # The notarization ticket is attached: prints "The validate action worked!" xcrun stapler validate "craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg" # The app, after you open the disk image: the signature must verify codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "/Volumes//Craft Anything.app" spctl --assess --type execute --verbose "/Volumes//Craft Anything.app" # The command-line tool: a bare program can't carry a ticket, so macOS checks it online codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2 ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli codesign -dv --verbose=4 ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli 2>&1 | grep Authority ``` The `Authority` lines should name a "Developer ID Application" certificate. If a check fails, don't run the file; report it with the output and the release tag. ### Linux | Format | x86_64 | aarch64 (ARM64) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | AppImage | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.AppImage` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.AppImage` | Runs anywhere; updates itself with [AppImageUpdate](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/AppImageUpdate) (`.zsync` files) | | Flatpak | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.flatpak` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.flatpak` | Sandboxed, so it can't start a browser on your computer, which studying websites needs (use another package for that); `flatpak install --user ` | | Debian/Ubuntu | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.deb` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.deb` | | | Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.rpm` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.rpm` | | | Tarball | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Unpack anywhere | RISC-V (riscv64): `craft-anything--linux-riscv64.tar.gz`, a tarball only. The AppImage carries the CLI too: run ` --cli ` (for example ` --cli mcp` for an MCP client), or make a link to the AppImage named `craft-anything-cli` and run that. ### FreeBSD | Build | File | |---|---| | x86_64 | `craft-anything--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | ### Web (WebAssembly) | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | Browser viewer | `craft-anything-web-.zip` | Says what a file is, in the browser (the file never leaves it); host the folder on any static web server ([packaging/web/README.md](packaging/web/README.md)) |

Come make things with us

Our Discord is where artists of every kind hang out: people who paint, shoot, draw, cut film, set type, and people still figuring out what they like to make. Share what you're working on, ask for help, tell us what's broken, or tell us what you wish these tools could do. Whatever your medium and however long you've been at it, you're welcome here.

items.readme_text:
T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it. ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` | | Windows | `winget install T3Tools.T3Code` or `scoop install extras/t3code` | | Arch Linux | `yay -S t3code-bin` | | Nix | `nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code` | | Debian, Ubuntu | `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases) | ### Command line This installs the `t3` command. Run `t3` to start the server and open the web app. ```bash curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex ``` To try it once without an install, run `npx t3@latest`. ### Phone Get the app from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code). Then follow [remote access](./docs/user/remote-access.md) to connect it to your computer. ### Sign in to an agent T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`, or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. [Provider setup](./docs/user/install.md#providers) has the steps for each agent. [Install T3 Code](./docs/user/install.md) covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS. ## "Wait, what are you selling me?" Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want. ## Documentation - [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md) - [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md) - [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md) - [Source control](./docs/user/source-control.md) - [Connect outside agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md) - [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md) [All docs](./docs/README.md) has the full list. ## Contributing We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first. - Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before you report a bug or open a pull request. - Put feature requests in [Ideas](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas). - Build from source with the [development runbook](./docs/operations/development.md#first-checkout). The [architecture overview](./docs/internals/overview.md) explains how it works. - Get help in [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

The frontier models are just there — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and the rest. > Free, with no usage cap.* > > 模型清单跟随上游刷新，可用性由**你自己这台机器的网络出口**实测得出， > 思考强度下发的是真实预算而不是提示词，另附一个 OpenAI 兼容的本地转发端口。 > > 纯插件挂载：不改内核、无构建步骤、零依赖。
--- ## 交流群

QQ 群：1132072680（AI技术交流群16）
扫码加入群聊，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。
--- ## 亮点 - **开箱即用，无配置环节**——不需要账号、不需要 Key、不需要在后台申请配额。 - **上游来源公开透明**——免费车道来源为 [OpenCode 的 Zen 网关](https://opencode.ai)，Kilo 渠道来源为 [Kilo AI 的公共网关](https://kilo.ai)，均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。 - **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。 - **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。 - **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。 - **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。 - **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。 - **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 `application/json` 的 content-type 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。插件按响应体形状判定，并将已嗅探的字节重新注入流，既不会导致整轮失败，也不会因 header 与实际内容不符而将可用模型判为不可用。 - **思考强度实际生效**——两类模型两种控制：声明了思考档位的模型（如 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、GLM 5.3 Flash）给出它自己的档位菜单（Off / Low / High / Max 等），选中值按原值下发到上游 `reasoning_effort`，上游会校验该字段、集合外的取值直接 400；没有档位菜单的模型（MiMo V2.6 等）走预算阶梯——Light / Balanced / Deep 对应输出 token 预算 2 048 / 8 192 / 模型上限，思考不可关闭的模型三档整体翻倍为 4 096 / 16 384 / 模型上限，因为思考与正文共享同一输出额度。两者都逐次调用留痕，设置页每张模型卡均标注档位或该档实际下发的上限（详见「思考强度：档位菜单与预算阶梯」）。 - **不依赖浏览器界面**——插件仅将 llm 作为硬依赖，在没有 web server 的 composition（如 dsh-tui）中同样完成启动并输出模型；看板模块挂载在独立的 fiber 上，待 webServer 就绪后再注册路由，因此既不会阻塞模型车道，也不会因插件先于 web 服务加载而永久丢失设置页。 - **用量看板，数据全部留在本机**——Token 热力图、总量曲线（支持总计与单模型视图）、输出速度与首字延迟逐次采样。不上传任何数据。 - **OpenAI 兼容转发端口**——本机其它工具通过 base URL 与 Key 即可调用这些模型。Chat 历史中 assistant 的字符串 `reasoning_content` 会随工具后续请求保留，包括显式空字符串；缺失字段不会被补造。 - **EAC 渠道（桌面端专属）**——在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端与 DSHEAC AIO 桌面端中自动解锁一条协付通道，模型以 EAC 前缀显示（如 EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash）；凭据加密密封，由宿主指纹闸门把守；该渠道在服务器侧校验 GitHub 授权（登录并 star 本仓库）后才放行对话；在命令行及其它宿主中该通道完全不存在。详见「EAC 渠道」。 - **Kilo 渠道（免密免费池）**——内置 Kilo AI 公共网关的免费模型池（`isFree` 清单实时拉取，含 `kilo-auto/free` 自动路由），无需任何账号或 Key；模型卡带 Kilo 徽章。思考强度与 EAC 渠道同款：模型自身的档位菜单（Off / Low / Medium / High，默认 High），经网关统一的 `reasoning` 参数真实下发——Off 已逐家族实测将思考归零（nemotron、ling、dots、poolside、apodex、cohere）；stepfun 与 liquid 端点强制思考（对关闭请求返回 400）、两个自动路由不透传关闭，这些模型的菜单不含 Off 档。该池由上游免费提供，上游会在其模型卡中声明 prompt 可能被记录用于改进服务——请勿发送敏感内容，详见「免责声明」。 - **聚合渠道，自带 Key**——设置页新增一页，把第三方端点接进同一条模型清单：注册表内置 76 家提供商（NVIDIA NIM、OpenRouter、Groq、Cerebras、SambaNova、Gemini、DeepSeek、Mistral、Together、Fireworks、SiliconFlow、Nebius、Chutes、Hugging Face、Cloudflare、Z.ai、Kimi、MiniMax、QwenCloud/Alibaba、Bedrock、Vertex、Vercel AI Gateway、Azure OpenAI、FleetRelay Gateway，以及无需账号的 Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp），写入 Key（本机免账号的提供商不需要）后其模型即以 `provider/model` 出现在选择器里，也可经本地网关调用。Key 只写入本机 0600 的 settings.json，API 只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹；每家可单独启停、测试（列表探测，不花一次生成）、发现模型、覆盖 Base URL 与模型清单。OAuth 与 ADC 认证的提供商照常列出，但标注为不可驱动。 - **省 Token**——三件事：工具输出压缩（RTK）在请求发出前就地重写 `tool_result`（git diff / status / log、grep、find、ls、tree、构建日志、编号转储、搜索清单、重复日志行），实测 40 KB 的 `git diff` 移除 90% 的字节且模型仍能就它作答；提示词瘦身有 caveman 与 ponytail 两族、默认全关；另有五个不占用上游请求的本地应答。设置页用与用量图表同一批统计行显示压缩前后字节、节省比例、压缩块数与统计调用数。 - **路由（降级链）**——把任意车道的模型串成一条命名链，以 `combo:` 作为虚拟模型出现在选择器与网关上；`fallback` 固定从链首开始，`round-robin` 轮换起点并连续 N 轮粘滞。链接在输出任何正文之前失败会被整段丢弃，切换对调用方不可见；思考增量不算正文，因此「想了很久才撞上配额墙」正是降级最有价值的场景。 - **本地网关原生说 Anthropic**——新增 `POST /v1/messages`（流式与非流式，含 thinking / tool_use 块、真实 stop_reason 与流内 error 事件）与 `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`（本地估算）；`/v1/models` 广播全部车道，含聚合行与链路。网关页新增「接入客户端」分区，按实际绑定的端口与真实要求的密钥生成 Claude Code、Codex、OpenAI SDK、Anthropic SDK、curl 与局域网的可复制配方。 - **接口具备鉴权围栏**——插件 HTTP 路由优先级高于内核 `/api`，因此内置与内核一致的信任检查（优先复用 composition 的 connection 服务，缺失时退回结构化围栏）。 - **十个账号渠道，一体接入**——LobsterAI（有道）、Qoder / Qoder 中国版（阿里系）、TRAE（字节）、Cline、Loomy（讯飞）、Raccoon（商汤）、MiniMax Code、ZCode（智谱）、Gemini（Google Code Assist）十个账号渠道开箱即用，外加 Kilo 免费车道与原匿名免费通道；OpenCode 账号渠道在本插件中默认停用。各渠道的登录流程、账号池、每日积分领取、模型黑名单与其本地 OpenAI 网关（Chat Completions + Responses，默认 `127.0.0.1:8326`）原样挂载与运行；凭据只写入宿主凭据库，浏览器永远拿不到明文。 - **视觉特效按需开启**——设置页顶部“视觉特效”开关默认关闭，鱼缸和业务功能始终保留；开启后恢复背景光晕、毛玻璃与装饰动画，选择仅保存在当前浏览器。 - **OFM 插件中心：渠道 / 增强 / 页面统一市场**——新仓库 [Ebony-Vinyl/ofm-extensions](https://github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/ofm-extensions) 承载社区插件：Ed25519 签名索引、安装即校验 SHA-256 与静态扫描、运行在 Worker VM 沙箱（唯一 import 是受控的 `ofm:sdk`，网络只放行 manifest 声明的域名，密钥只进不出，每个 hook 带超时熔断）。渠道插件装上即出现在模型选择器（支持 `replaces` 接管内置车道），增强插件以 `onRequest`/`onModels`/`onUsage` 挂进请求链；页面插件在侧边栏贡献一个沙箱 iframe 页面，只能通过受控消息桥读写自己的配置与存储。清单 v1 与 v2 双兼容；内置账号渠道包、聚合渠道目录、客户端启动器、资源库格式与模型工作台也以 built-in 描述符登记在同一插件中心，不可卸载但可查看贡献。发现、安装、更新、启停、配置、密钥、自检、卸载全部在控制台「插件中心」完成；开发者模式可安装本地未签名包（显式风险确认、未验证徽标、同一沙箱）。市场页另带封面横幅、类型色带与骨架屏，详情弹层含签名源码直达链接、发布说明（changelog）与权限清单；索引由宿主后台定时刷新，已装插件的清单可一键导出 / 导入（JSON，不含密钥）用于迁移。模型工作台（magpie）车道的推理请求也接入同一增强钩子链（onRequest），并默认经宿主可替换的 fetch 出站，本机代理类插件（如上下文扩展）重新可见；OFM_ENGINE_PRIVATE_FETCH=1 可回到私有直连。 - **免费车道额度断路器与出口代理（issue #708/#767 的完整回答）**——上游按出口 IP 计免费配额，一次真实 429 即开窗（`Retry-After` 缺省 6 小时），窗口内本插件本地拒绝新回合、不再向墙上送请求；`FreeTierError` 单独锁道。手动测试全部保留（清单刷新/单模型检测/测速），自动探测依旧禁用——状态从真实回合被动学习。车道可配独立出口代理（http/https/socks5），也认 `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` 环境变量；「换出口后重试一次」一键清窗，「测试出口」打第三方回显不花配额。请求形状对齐官方 2.2.3 客户端（`traceparent`/`b3`/通配 `accept`），并移植 opencode2api v1.4.7 的工具名绑定、幽灵调用清理与标题请求免整形。 - **十三页毛玻璃界面**——设置页顶部导航扩为十一个页面：原有六页（**免费模型**（鱼缸水位 = 可用模型占比）、**EAC 模型**（鱼缸水位 = 协付池压力）、**白嫖模型接入**（十张渠道卡：登录、账号、模型开关、一键领取积分）、**数据看板**（今日/全部 Token 消耗、平均生成速度、缓存命中率、成功率，账号透视与模型性能表、最近请求总览）、**运行日志**（逐请求明细：结果、耗时、首字、速度、Token 细分，失败原因悬停可见）与**网关设置**（网关开关/端点/密钥；局域网转发中继：监听地址、端口与独立中继密钥）），新增**聚合渠道**（提供商注册表、Key、测试、发现模型、Base URL 与模型清单覆盖）、**省 Token**（压缩开关、两族提示词档位、五个本地应答与节省统计）、**路由**（降级链编辑器）、**插件升级**（版本检查、一键升级与热重载）与**推荐项目**（EAC-Desktop / EAC-Pack / EAC-design-world 三张卡片：简介、直达链接与 Star 按钮，Star / Fork / 最近提交数实时取自 GitHub，取不到就整块不显示）五页；网关设置页另增「接入客户端」分区。页面切换与卡片入场为 150–250 ms 短动效，`prefers-reduced-motion` 下整体关闭。每页都有直达 GitHub 仓库的 Star 按钮。 - **局域网转发中继**——渠道网关本身只监听本机（上游的安全选择）；本插件提供自己的转发门：调用方用插件签发与轮换的中继密钥，转发跳由宿主换用网关凭据（凭据不出宿主进程），仅放行 `/v1/*` 模型接口并带环路保护。 ## 你会看到什么 **输入框的模型选择器** | 分组 | 内容 | | --- | --- | | Our Free Model | 当前网络出口可直接使用的模型 | | 使用各渠道即表示你同意对应上游的服务条款与用量政策；因违反上游政策导致的限流、封禁或其它后果由使用者自行承担。插件不对任何上游的可用性、准确性或连续性作任何承诺。 - **EAC 渠道为协付性质。** 该渠道的凭据与网关由仓库维护者部署（GitHub 登录 + star 仓库解锁），仅限授权用户使用；请勿尝试绕过授权闸门，勿转售或共享渠道访问权——滥用会导致全体用户的通道被收紧。 - **本插件与上述任何上游厂商无隶属或背书关系。** 各厂商名称与商标归其各自所有者所有，仅在说明来源时引用。 ## 安全与隐私 所有状态写入 DSH_HOME/our-free-model/；用量与设置仅落在本机，不上传至任何位置。 聚合车道的 Key 同样不出本机：它只写入插件自己的 0600 `settings.json`，请求只发往你自己配置的那家提供商，插件接口只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹，从不回显 Key 本身；测试与发现模型两次探测也把回包中的 Key 一律脱敏。 转发监听仅绑定回环地址，默认 127.0.0.1，无 Key 请求一律拒绝。将地址改为可路由接口会被直接拒绝（POST /settings 返回 400 并注明原因；在无 web server 的 composition 中手工写入 settings.json 同样不会启动监听）——该端口的流量消耗的是本机这条免密车道，不应由一个字符串决定是否向整个子网开放。 局域网访问是另开的一扇门，并不放宽上述规则：本机监听仍只绑回环、修改地址仍被拒绝；需要跨机器使用时必须显式启用"局域网访问"，中继绑定可路由地址，且每个请求都需携带局域网 Key——连 /、/health 这类存活探针也一并鉴权（仅本机监听免 Key 应答存活探测），否则一个未鉴权的应答等同于向整个子网宣告"该主机正在代理"。中继仅转发 /v1/models、/v1/chat/completions、/v1/responses、/v1/messages、/v1/messages/count_tokens 五条白名单路径（各自的去 /v1 写法同样放行），不代理任意 loopback 服务；入口处将局域网 Key 换为本机 Key，因此两把 Key 互不通用；携带跳数标记的请求直接拒绝（508），因此端口即使配置为本机监听的同一端口也不会自环。局域网 Key 同样由 crypto 生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于同一 0600 文件中，可在面板上单独轮换。 转发 Key 由 crypto 运行时生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于 0600 权限文件中。本仓库不含任何硬编码凭据。/ 与 /health 为存活探针，先于 Key 检查应答，但仅回答"是否在线"，获取模型清单仍需 Key。 插件的 HTTP 路由带请求信任围栏（自 v1.1 修复）：插件的 /api/our-free-model 前缀在 webServer 的最长前缀分发下优先于内核 /api，曾绕过内核鉴权。当前每个请求先经由 composition 的 connection 服务准入（与内核 /api 完全同级的 cookie/token 校验）；connection 缺失的 composition 退回结构化围栏——loopback Host、拒绝跨站 sec-fetch-site、Origin/Referer 必须与 Host 同源同端口，Host 缺失或为空也拒绝（fail closed，不回退至 socket 本地地址）。实测结果：异源 Host/Origin 返回 403，无 cookie 的回环请求返回 401。connection 为逐请求获取，因为浏览器半身要到插件加载之后才将其 provide 出来——若在 apply 时以快照方式读取一次，围栏会在整个进程周期内退化为结构化那一层（本轮将该读取改回快照后，picker-test 的 401 断言立即失败）。 公告 HTML 在客户端经严格白名单渲染：scripts/sanitize-test.mjs 使用 XSS 语料（脚本注入、事件属性、javascript:/data: URL、iframe/svg/form、样式注入、畸形标签）验证全部被丢弃；不经过任何 innerHTML sink。公告源的 feedUrl 可被用户指向任意 URL，因此渲染器按不可信输入处理。 应用内升级的完整性链（v1.3.2 加签）：清单 Ed25519 签名验证（公钥 pin 在 src/updater.js，无签名或验签失败的清单直接拒绝，未签名镜像不会被安装）→ 清单校验（semver、路径逃逸、哈希格式、base 必须为清单相对路径）→ 下载时逐文件校验 SHA-256 与字节数 → staging 回读校验 → 安装后回读校验 → 任一步失败即恢复备份；安装前强制重新拉取清单，杜绝陈旧清单。文件与代码边界见已知边界一节。 更新通道与 feedUrl 彻底解耦（v1.3.2）：feedUrl 仅重定向公告 feed，永不再重定向升级清单——此前一个设置项即可将升级源指向任意服务器并配以自配平的哈希，等同于将"修改一个设置值"升级为"在宿主进程中执行任意代码"。公告 override 本身也收紧为仅 https（回环 http 除外，本机镜像与测试仍可用）且不得内嵌凭据。目标域不受限制：任何 https 地址均可作为 feedUrl，插件按 feedPollMinutes 的间隔轮询——因此在不含 connection 服务的 composition 中（见上文鉴权说明），能够修改设置的本机调用者可让进程持续请求任意外部地址。这与插件的其余外联一样按"设置即信任"对待：能够修改 settings.json 的人本来就能安装代码。 转发监听仅绑回环地址，且按解析结果绑定（v1.3.2）：localhost 这类主机名先经 dns.lookup 解析、全部结果均为回环才放行，绑定使用解析出的 IP——当 hosts 文件或企业 DNS 将 localhost 指向可路由接口时，校验与监听不再各自为政。 卸载只需移除 bundle 条目，插件不留任何补丁；其数据目录为纯 JSON，可直接删除。 ## 许可证 MIT，见 LICENSE。 本项目为独立插件，与任何模型提供方无隶属、认可或赞助关系。使用该插件访问免费额度受各提供方 自身条款约束；在超出个人机器的场景中部署前，请先确认这些条款。 ## Star 趋势 图表由 Star History 自动更新，无需手动提交图片。受服务缓存（当前为 24 小时）和 GitHub 图片缓存影响，显示可能延迟，并非秒级实时；点击图表可查看在线趋势。

Claude Cage

**把 Claude 大小姐关起来，为了更好地保护我们的相遇** [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage?include_prereleases)](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage/releases) [![CI](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) **[项目主页](https://claude-cage.com/) · [下载应用](https://claude-cage.com/#download) · [使用文档](https://claude-cage.com/docs/) · [常见问题](https://claude-cage.com/docs/troubleshooting/)** [简体中文](README.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [العربية](README.ar.md) · [فارسی](README.fa.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [မြန်မာဘာသာ](README.my.md) · [Беларуская](README.be.md) · [پښتو](README.ps.md) · [دری](README.prs.md) · [አማርኛ](README.am.md) · [Soomaali](README.so.md) · [ትግርኛ](README.ti.md) · [Français](README.fr.md)
## 受够了 Anthropic 作为一个只是想和 Claude 对话与合作的正常用户，受够了折腾各种 VPS，指纹浏览器，环境检测，面对封号的担惊受怕和财产损失。我们提出 **Claude Cage** 项目：**一个开箱即用的桌面程序，配置好自己的网络代理，集中管理隔离环境、时区语言和环境检查。** Claude Cage 让你在熟悉的系统里与 Claude 一起工作：Mac 上用 macOS 虚拟机，Windows 上用 Windows 虚拟机，也可以选择轻量的 Linux 环境。终端、浏览器、编辑器和官方 Claude Desktop 汇集在同一个工作台，项目按需共享，网络独立管理；还可以连接自己的服务器，或用手机接续电脑上的任务。支持以下几个重点功能： - 和主机隔离的网络设置，Cage 自己接管和代理内部的所有网络流量 - 和主机隔离的指纹设置，包括时区、语言等，支持自动与代理 IP 同步 - 针对 Claude 使用过程中的全链路适配（浏览器登录，授权，claude code 进程） - 内置网络与隔离检查，关键检查失败或证据不完整时暂停外网；社区和第三方检测提供补充参考 **使用 Cage 的环境检测结果：** | 网络与隔离检查 | 浏览器环境检测（社区参考） | | :---: | :---: | | | | [FuckClaude](https://fuck-claude.vercel.app/) · [LinXiaoTao / GitHub](https://github.com/LinXiaoTao/FuckClaude) **Cage 运行主界面：** ![Cage](www/public/workbench-2026-11.jpg) ## 你可以用它做什么 - **在一个窗口里完成工作。** 用终端运行 Claude Code，用编辑器查看改动，用 Cage 浏览器预览服务和完成登录。 - **用熟悉的系统开发。** 选择 macOS、Windows 或 Linux 客机，使用对应平台的工具；也可自动匹配本机系统版本，下载官方镜像并创建独立环境。 [选择客机系统](docs/guide/guest-systems.md) - **控制共享范围。** 只共享默认工作区和明确打开的项目文件夹；主机的 Claude 登录、浏览器配置和 SSH 密钥不会自动导入。 - **看清网络状态。** 内置代理管理支持导入订阅、选择节点和检查出口。关键检查未通过时，环境保持离线；代理不可用时没有直连回退。 - **下次继续使用。** 工具、文件和登录状态保存在虚拟磁盘里，关闭窗口可以保留后台任务。 - **管理多个 Claude Code 订阅。** 查看额度、为新会话分配账号，并在明确授权后切换账号接续历史。 [Claude Code](docs/guide/accounts.md) - **从手机继续处理任务。** Android / iPhone 配对电脑，接续 Claude Code 对话与工具审批，或操作远程浏览器和 Claude Desktop。[手机连接](docs/guide/mobile.md) - **把环境放到自己的服务器。** 通过 SSH 部署或连接 Linux VPS，工具、任务和数据留在服务器，无需 KVM。[云端部署与 SSH](docs/guide/cloud.md) - **通过私网连接设备。** 在 Cage 内登录 Tailscale，查看网络中的设备，使用 SSH、Web 与其他 TCP 服务。 [Tailscale 私网](docs/guide/tailscale.md) 浏览器收藏、无痕会话、Cookie、扩展、密码保险箱，以及外观、资源、存储和工具更新，见[完整使用文档](https://claude-cage.com/docs/)。 ## 快速开始 把这句话发给你的 agent（codex，dsh，workbuddy，反正不会是 claude code😁） ```markdown 帮我安装 https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage ，并把 Cage 的代理配置为我本机 Clash 的 xxx 节点。 ``` 你唯一需要的，是一个靠谱的代理节点，本项目不做任何代理推广，可以自行搜索黑色错误网站解决。 ## 下载与安装 Cage 支持 macOS、Windows 和 Linux：macOS 14+ 的 Apple Silicon Mac、Windows 10 22H2 / 11 x64，以及 Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 x86_64。Windows 11 客机需要支持 Hyper-V 的 Windows 11 专业版、企业版或教育版主机；其他受支持的 Windows 主机可使用 Debian 或 Ubuntu 22.04。Intel Mac、Windows ARM64 和 Linux ARM64 暂不支持。 [macOS](docs/getting-started.md) · [Windows](docs/windows.md) · [Linux](docs/linux.md)。 1. 打开[项目主页](https://claude-cage.com/#download)，点击“下载应用”并选择平台。 2. macOS：打开安装包，将 **Cage** 拖入 **Applications（应用程序）**，再从“应用程序”启动。Windows：[安装说明](docs/windows.md#安装并开始工作) · Linux：[安装说明](docs/linux.md#安装并开始工作)。 3. 按应用内引导配置自己的代理，启动环境后打开项目。 安装包随附工作台和代理核心，无需先安装 Go、Node.js、Docker 或 Clash。首次创建环境时选择客机系统与存储位置，再准备对应的官方系统镜像和开发工具。macOS、Windows 系统按各自许可使用；Cage 不提供系统授权、代理服务或 Claude 账户。 源码与安装包公开，版本说明和校验文件见 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage/releases)。系统选择、镜像来源与数据保留方式见[客机系统指南](docs/guide/guest-systems.md)。 功能以所用构建为准，公开安装包的能力与验证范围以发行说明为准。 macOS 和已签名 Windows 版本支持通过所选代理更新；Windows 未签名预览版与 Linux 使用安装包手动更新。更新前保存并停止任务，个人数据继续保留。 [升级与卸载](docs/guide/maintenance.md) ## 三步开始 ### 1. 选择代理 导入 Clash/Mihomo YAML 订阅或本地配置，选择节点并点击“应用代理”；需要中转时可配置链式代理。[网络与代理](docs/guide/network.md) ### 2. 启动环境 首次选择客机系统或“自动匹配本机系统版本”，再选择存储位置。点击“安装客户机”或“启动 Cage 环境”，按引导完成安装与授权；进度和错误可在“操作详情”查看。以后启动复用原环境。 ### 3. 打开项目，运行 Claude 点击“打开项目”选择本机上的文件夹，再新建终端，输入 `claude`，在 Cage 浏览器中完成自己的账户授权。也可以先使用默认工作区，无需提前准备项目。完整步骤见[开始使用](docs/getting-started.md)。 ## 使用前了解这些边界 - 共享项目中的修改和删除直接影响本机原文件，包括 Git 操作。请使用版本控制或备份，并核对提交结果。 - 同一份 Cage 配置中的项目共用所选客机系统、工具、账户与文件系统，项目之间没有独立隔离。更换客机系统需要独立安装，原环境的数据继续保留。 - 默认公网出站支持 IPv4 TCP，DNS 通过同一代理；公网 UDP、IPv6、ICMP 及主机和局域网直连受限。主动启用 Tailscale 后，可按私网权限连接设备。 -
